title: Target Compatibility and Stability
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of target compatibility and stability using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates target compatibility and stability.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Target Compatibility and Stability** as part of **Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, and Kotlin/Native**. Kotlin Multiplatform organizes shared logic and target-specific implementations through source sets; only APIs available for every configured target belong in common code. Use the subtopics—Platform Support and Toolchain Requirements, Stable, Beta, and Experimental Features, Choosing a Platform for Production—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-platform targets differ in runtime APIs, toolchains, and support maturity. Check the current compatibility matrix before committing to a production target.

items.title: Platform Support and Toolchain Requirements
items.text: Platform Support and Toolchain Requirements is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

items.title: Stable, Beta, and Experimental Features
items.text: Stable, Beta, and Experimental Features is one part of target compatibility and stability. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, or Kotlin/Native project configured for the selected target. Verify platform support and maturity before production use.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Target Compatibility and Stability removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
